focus: Connect the verified native input collectors to browser commands and automatic replay capture/playback, completing actor integration.
note: The game is playable, but the offline rewrite is not yet equivalent to Worms Armageddon. Verified routines can still be waiting for live integration.

areas.title: Worm movement & physics
areas.live: Native collision masks, jump flight, hurt motion, drowning and several recovery paths are integrated. Fresh worm initialization now matches original spawn selection, state fields, gravity-derived thresholds, labels, ownership slots and placement retry ordering against full constructor memory captures. Physics/placement/state-entry adapters still need live composition. Fresh worm construction now defaults to native physics-memory initialization and shares resource setup with replay restoration; composed constructor captures also verify the registration-time body state. Environment membership, placement and state entry still need composition. The fresh worm factory now composes task attachment/registration and native environment membership, verified with original constructor/list-insertion captures. Spawn providers, placement and state entry remain adapters. Fresh worm construction now uses recovered weighted/side spawn selection, reservation and a separate spawn random stream, verified in native constructor sequences. Landgen candidate generation is separately verified; live match integration remains. Authored maps now use native candidate generation and weighted spawn selection; live worm construction and settling remain host adapters. Authored-map startup now shares the verified native constructor placement block; full actor state/resource/task construction remains.
areas.remaining: Complete the movement/state lifecycle, ground interactions and collision ordering; compare full movement sequences with the original.

areas.title: Weapons & inventory
areas.live: Original weapon data and many projectile, melee, hitscan and placed-weapon routines drive live play. Teleport searches nearby valid positions using the original worm mask and collision registry. Live girders now use original target bounds, Manhattan range from the default native scheme, and sprite collision checks against current terrain and bodies. Rejected placement preserves ammo and terrain. Girder shape cycling, scheme overrides and native targeting commands remain. Native weapon selection now composes descriptor input flags, arsenal closure, targeting ownership transitions and bounds against executable fixtures. Live browser selection and full team-event dispatch remain to connect. Default weapon selection now reproduces saved choices, deployment teleport and state-dependent fallback scans, and composes with native worm selection. Live inventory and task adapters remain. Post-shot cleanup and deferred weapon selection now match native execution, including selection-before-ammo ordering and busy-state retention; live controller integration remains. Native firing notifications now match multi-shot ammo rules, remaining-shot announcement selection and final-shot targeting release; live wiring remains. Native activation now defaults to the executable-verified70-slot weapon-delay countdown, including unlock announcement RNG and sound ordering; live inventory/presentation wiring remains.
areas.remaining: Finish every weapon state machine, scheme override, special-availability rule, ammo-loading path and utility delay lifecycle.

areas.title: Damage & destruction
areas.live: Native blast, crater, damage accounting, flames and crate/barrel behavior are substantially integrated.
areas.remaining: Complete event ordering and remaining collision/chain-reaction paths, then validate composed sequences against native matches.

areas.title: Rope & utilities
areas.live: Recovered rope launch, swing, release and refire behavior is integrated alongside original utility art and several utility actions.
areas.remaining: Finish native control and state transitions for jetpack, parachute, teleport, girders, freeze and other utilities; verify their interactions.

areas.title: Turns & match rules
areas.live: Native team/worm rotation, wind selection, settlement presentation, poison settlement and recurring environment effects are integrated. Native controller worm-selection reset and ordered actor notifications now match executable fixtures, including input-mode and pointer-ownership cleanup; live controller integration remains. Controller block, resume and deactivation events now match native ownership, input-mode, ammo-settlement and camera/AI cleanup sequences; activation now also matches original input ownership, default-selection requests and human/AI branch ordering. Worm cycling, timer cancellation, arsenal closure and action-counter events also match native fixtures. Child-task dispatch, delay presentation and live integration remain. Post-shot cleanup and deferred weapon selection now match native execution, including selection-before-ammo ordering and busy-state retention; live controller integration remains. Native activation now defaults to the executable-verified70-slot weapon-delay countdown, including unlock announcement RNG and sound ordering; live inventory/presentation wiring remains. Native frame dispatch now composes deferred selection, camera requests and selection countdown with verified update order, sound gates and fixed-point smoothing. Camera focus and pause collectors now also match the executable and run by default, including queried worm coordinates, key consumption and ownership gates. Presentation state updates now also match native smoothing, panel and arsenal-refresh behavior; widget drawing and live browser adapters remain. Native child forwarding and addressed task sends now match mutable traversal and registry behavior; the controller task entry forwards unhandled events to children. Live actor dispatch integration remains. Controller addressed routes now default to native registry sends, preserving sender and payload metadata; composed movement, block, timer and worm-transfer sequences match the executable. Live actor handlers remain. Fresh native team-controller initialization now matches state defaults, worm creation order, failure handling and registration requests; resource setup is shared with replay restoration. The fresh controller factory now attaches to its parent and registers through recovered logical task construction, preserving child order/capacity and shared registries. Live worm/resource constructors remain adapters.
areas.remaining: Connect the complete native turn controller, action-busy ownership, retreat requests, input gates and scheme rules.

areas.title: Maps & terrain
areas.live: Original authored maps, terrain objects, collision masks and animated water are available in the game. Authored maps use native candidate discovery, fallback terrain carving/platforms, pool trimming and weighted worm spawn selection. Natural mines and barrels reserve positions from that pool before worm creation, using original default-scheme count/mix/fuse. Mines use native timer/body initialization, downward settling, slope sampling and shared registration; barrels use their native constructor. All100 authored maps pass the existing six-worm grounding/separation checks. Worms now use the native constructor placement sequence directly, replacing the simulated startup drop on authored maps.
areas.remaining: Connect host presets to their native scheme settings, native side placement and complete procedural landscape generation; finish terrain-theme behavior and terrain history/dirty-region handling. Full worm task/state/resource construction and water/seed conversion still use host adapters.

areas.title: Sprites, animation & HUD
areas.live: Original media, native animation routines and many HUD elements are integrated, including the animated wind meter. Live idle rendering uses original healthy/low-health breathing, poison entry/loop and cure/heal transitions. Inactive grounded worms use simulation-driven original weighted gestures, position-derived cooldown, logic RNG and owned cough audio; the wall-clock blink trigger is removed. Direct-hit and blast damage now feed the original idle reaction latch:25 selects accusation,26 selects the fist gesture, and selection clears the latch. Scheduler memory participates in actor snapshots. Native controller panel sliding, arsenal refresh, selection countdown, targeting markers and aim-cursor drawing are executable-verified and run in the native render pass, but their complete live canvas/font/resource adapters remain unfinished. Full actor eligibility, surrender/marked-team states, animation scheduling and render-task lifecycle still need integration. The native worm draw request now matches1008 executable captures for action layers, draw rank and poison/team flags; shared browser draw-queue and pose-resolver integration remain. Native pose resolution now reproduces175 slope-aware strips, special-state progress and facing, verified in4497 direct and4497 composed draw captures. The native draw routine defaults to this resolver; live browser adapters remain. Live idle and equipped poses now use the recovered pose resolver with original uphill/downhill sprites and facing. Simulation-driven native ground sampling and slope hysteresis are verified against1458 executable cases; special-action render branches and complete draw-queue integration remain. Preparation, recoil, axe, Fire Punch, drill and blowtorch now share the native pose resolver. Blowtorch rendering uses its original aim-dependent strip and saved-X draw position. Remaining movement/death/utility render paths and the shared draw queue still need integration. Walking, jumping, landing, recovery, hurt/death and non-jetpack utility poses now also use the native resolver. Walking uses its original cycle X anchor, and flight/teleport use native position/progress transforms. Jetpack composite rendering, shared queue ordering/flags and full actor lifecycle remain. Jetpack flame requests are now executable-verified and drive live composition with native body facing, flames behind the worm and absolute-position pixel truncation. The composite canvas and shared scene queue remain browser adapters. Native sprite-queue insertion, original bundled sort (including equal-key ordering), limits and projection now match full executable sequences. Jetpack composition uses this queue; scene-wide submission, other primitive types and palette flags remain unfinished. Crate sprite/content/countdown draw orchestration now matches640 executable sequences, including priority, blinking and submersion gates; live crate label, rank and scene-queue adapters remain to connect. Crate draw requests now compose with native mixed image/sprite queue allocation, sorting and projection across640 executable sequences. Live browser text and full scene integration remain unfinished. The shared native text-image cache now matches576 executable calls for borders, clipping, cache invalidation, fade image selection and seed updates. Font/image backends and live crate/HUD use remain to connect. Live announcements now use the recovered text-image cache through a browser font/image backend, preserving cache state across messages and using original gray borders and clipping. Crate/other HUD use, complete indexed drawing and presentation-cache replay integration remain. Live crates now use native body/label draw requests, the mixed queue and text backend, with center anchors, pixel snapping and shared rank allocation/release. Content labels remain gated off until native reveal-setting ownership is connected; full scene ordering and presentation-resource lifecycle remain unfinished.
areas.remaining: Finish the complete animation state graph, remaining poses and HUD transitions, renderer/task visibility and native scheduling.

areas.title: Sound & speech
areas.live: Original samples, speech banks and several native sound queues, loops and event triggers are integrated.
areas.remaining: Complete sound ownership, priorities, speech selection and remaining event triggers across all actor states.

areas.title: Computer opponents
areas.live: A playable computer opponent is present. Its host heuristics are not a complete port of the original AI.
areas.remaining: Port native movement planning, trajectory search, weapon selection and difficulty behavior.

areas.title: Setup, missions & progression
areas.live: Local match setup, authored-map selection, schemes and series play are available.
areas.remaining: Reproduce native team setup, saved schemes, missions, training and campaign progression.

areas.title: Replays & local saves
areas.live: The public replay remains a trajectory overlay. Native input, frame, dispatch, session, snapshot and audio routines compose into executable-verified pipelines. Development capture reads live actor, controller, terrain, palette and random state without changing the match; sound-enabled restore reproduces tested sequences for eight weapons, restores water/nuclear presentation and preserves player records and mute. Live replay entry uses native audio cleanup. Menu, movement, weapon, arsenal-pointer and targeting collectors now reproduce native command bytes and call ordering; the controller defaults to these collectors. Targeting includes shape/direction cycling, cursor bounds, packed placement coordinates and follow-up actions. Targeting teardown now clears flags and releases pointer ownership through the original routine, verified directly and inside the collector. Targeting entry also reproduces original cursor initialization, camera requests and priority ownership acquisition; its live selection adapter remains. These collectors still need browser mapping and automatic capture/playback integration. A native receiver now handles 45 movement, setting, cursor, target, weapon-selection and controller lifecycle command types against executable fixtures. Remaining lifecycle events and downstream live task dispatch are still incomplete. Native task dispatch is verified against executable captures and composes with controller fallback forwarding; actor handler integration remains.
areas.remaining: Verify the remaining actor round trips, and connect rendering/game-state adapters; replace the overlay with deterministic replay and local saves.

areas.title: Determinism & whole-match parity
areas.live: A 50 Hz simulation and native random streams underpin many executable-verified routines.
areas.remaining: Finish original input queues, dispatch order and random-call ordering; compare representative complete matches with the original executable.
